After: E and F are gone, shown dashed. Their outside edge from D now attaches to B, and the edges inside the group collapse into one self-loop on B." width="100%"} Merges all specified nodes into the first node in the list. All edges incident to any of the contracted nodes are redirected to the first node. Edges between contracted nodes become self-loops (if `self_loops=True`). This generalizes `contract_nodes()` and `contracted_edge()` to a whole group at once, and the nodes do not need to be adjacent. Use it to collapse a set of nodes that should be treated as one unit, for example: - summarizing a detected community, department, or region as a single node while keeping its links to the rest of the network - merging duplicate records of the same entity (entity resolution) - simplifying a dense cluster before layout or further analysis Edges at the merged node that end up connecting the same pair of nodes are collapsed into one (the first one found keeps its weight and attributes), and all edges inside the group collapse into at most one self-loop. Edges between other nodes, parallel ones included, are kept as they are. The remaining nodes keep their IDs, labels and attributes, and surviving edges keep their IDs. The original graph is not modified. To collapse *every* group of a partition in one step, use `quotient_graph()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs or labels to contract. The first node is the target; all other nodes are merged into it, so it keeps its ID and label. Entries should be unique: repeating the first node raises a `ValueError` and repeating another node raises a `KeyError`. A single-element list returns an unchanged copy. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between contracted nodes become self-loops. If `False`, such edges are removed. Use `False` when the internal connections of the group are not of interest or when later algorithms do not handle self-loops. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with all specified nodes contracted into one. It has `len(nodes) - 1` fewer nodes than the original. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any node ID does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node list is empty, if a label is not found, or if the first node appears again later in the list. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Repeated contraction costs $O(k \cdot E)$ for $k$ nodes: each merge scans the current edge list, and after each merge the graph is one node smaller. The head of the list is the surviving node, inheriting every edge that touched any member of the batch; the remaining nodes disappear along with their labels and attributes, while the survivor keeps its own. This is the natural building block for community-quotienting workflows where an entire cluster collapses to a single representative before further analysis. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Contracting three consecutive nodes of a six-node path leaves four nodes: ::: {#857b43db .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(6) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 -- 6 result = g.contract_nodes_multi([2, 3, 4]) result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: A triangle "A", "B", "C" with a tail to "D" collapses into a single node "A". The three triangle edges become one self-loop, and the link to "D" is kept: ::: {#1c55e159 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")]) g.contract_nodes_multi(["A", "B", "C"]).get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A--A', 'A--D'] ``` ::: ::: With `self_loops=False`, the group's internal edges are discarded: ::: {#db20926d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.contract_nodes_multi(["A", "B", "C"], self_loops=False).get_edges_str_repr( use_labels=True ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A--D'] ``` ::: ::: This is especially useful for collapsing a detected community down to a single representative node. Here the first community found by Louvain in two triangles joined by a bridge is merged into one node, leaving the other triangle intact: ::: {#3f08b46b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) membership = g.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) community = sorted(n for n, c in membership.items() if c == membership[1]) simplified = g.contract_nodes_multi(community, self_loops=False) simplified.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['A--D', 'D--E', 'E--F', 'F--D'] ``` ::: :::
